title: P1 — redirect()/revalidatePath() run INSIDE the withTenantScope body at 12 files, and nothing establishes or enforces the invariant that they must live outside it
why_open: The invariant is stated nowhere and enforced nowhere. `withTenantScope` (apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:409-418) documents only 'the wrapper has to enclose *all* of the body' (tenant-scope.ts:398-401) — the exact opposite advice for navigation calls — and `runInTenantScope` (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts:105-123, line numbers as of the current working tree) wraps the callback in `settleInsideContext` (context.ts:98), so a Next.js control-flow throw unwinds out through the AsyncLocalStorage frame. I scanned every `withTenantScope(` body in the tree with a paren-balancing walk: 12 files put a navigation call inside it. redirect(): apps/web/src/app/(app)/admin/actions.ts:73, apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/actions.ts:168, apps/web/src/app/(app)/messages/actions.ts:135,190,224,255,319, apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/documents/actions.ts:113,214, apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:490. revalidatePath(): admin/actions.ts:499-501,896-898,920,942,965, calendar/actions.ts:166-167, feed/actions.ts:51,84,154,233, orgs/actions.ts:46,102-104,142-144,159-161, orgs/[slug]/documents/actions.ts:82,149,184, orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:93,104,133,199,290,318,489, orgs/[slug]/members/actions.ts:121,189, orgs/[slug]/memory/actions.ts:62, resources/actions.ts:68-69,85-86, settings/actions.ts:164,190. (apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:181-182,500-505 also does it and is owned by another run — leave it alone.) I also ran a second scan for a navigation call lexically inside a `db.$transaction(` callback and found NONE today, so no write is being rolled back at this instant — but every one of these files calls `db.$transaction` in the same body (admin/actions.ts:244,471,693; calendar/actions.ts:80; messages/actions.ts:102,287,351; orgs/actions.ts:31; orgs/[slug]/documents/actions.ts:56; orgs/[slug]/finance/actions.ts:122,158,263,306,431; orgs/[slug]/memory/actions.ts:38; settings/actions.ts:146,177), so the next person to move a redirect one block up gets a silent rollback with a successful navigation. No test guards it: `tests/architecture/` has 15 specs and none mention redirect; apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.test.ts:248 only comments that 'redirect() and notFound() are thrown, so swallowing here would break' and asserts nothing about placement. The React.cache() half of finding #16 is in better shape but still unstated: every cache()d function in apps/web either keys on the tenant (config/server.ts:34,89,136 and institution-time.ts:17 key on institutionId; tenant-scope.ts:352 returns a TenantScope, not rows) or is deliberate auth-bootstrap (rbac.ts:42 getUserContext, tenant-scope.ts:58 institutionCandidates, tenant-scope.ts:248 actingInstitutions over PLATFORM_GLOBAL Institution). Nothing stops the next one from returning tenant rows keyed only on userId. PREREQUISITE / CROSS-RUN COLLISION, verified in the working tree at survey time and NOT caused by this survey: a concurrent run has added a REQUIRED `environment: PaymentMode` to `TenantScope` (apps/web/src/lib/tenancy/context.ts:17-35) and a hard refusal in `runInTenantScope` (context.ts:115-121, `if (!isPaymentMode(scope.environment)) throw`), but has not updated the three real construction sites — apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:165-170 `scopeForUser` (every user page and every server action), apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:433-436 `withSystemTenantScope` (every job, and `forEachInstitution` through it), and apps/web/src/lib/platform/tenant-export.ts:124-127. `git status --porcelain` shows context.ts modified and tenant-scope.ts untouched. As the tree stands every `withTenantScope` call throws `TenantContextError` before the body runs — a total outage, and the exact type-widening failure mode the brief warns about. Whoever implements this item edits tenant-scope.ts and will hit it on the first test run: check whether the owning run has landed the fix before touching those lines, and do NOT silently default `environment` to paper over it.
smallest_real_change: Two halves, both required. (a) Make the scope hand its result back so navigation happens after it closes: every one of the 12 files becomes `const x = await withTenantScope(userId, async () => { ...; return { slug } })` followed by `revalidatePath(...); redirect(...)` at the action's top level. `withTenantScope` already returns `Promise<T>` (tenant-scope.ts:409-413) and `settleInsideContext` (context.ts:77-81) already forces the thenable to settle inside the store, so no signature change is needed — only moving the last statements out of the callback. Do NOT touch apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts. (b) State and enforce the invariant. Add `tests/architecture/navigation-outside-tenant-scope.test.mjs` (node:test, the shape the other 15 specs in that directory use — `git ls-files` + read + assert) that paren-balances each `withTenantScope(`/`runInTenantScope(`/`withSystemTenantScope(` callback in apps/** and fails on any `redirect(`, `notFound(`, `revalidatePath(` or `revalidateTag(` inside it, naming file:line and quoting why (a Next control-flow throw inside `db.$transaction` aborts the transaction). Same spec asserts no `cache(`-wrapped export in apps/web/src/lib returns a value the tenancy registry classifies as TENANT_SCOPED unless its first parameter is an institutionId. MUTATION PROOF: move `redirect(\`/messages/${convo.id}\`)` from messages/actions.ts back inside the `withTenantScope` callback, run the new spec, confirm it reds naming messages/actions.ts; restore; confirm green. Mutate the PRODUCER not the helper — the assertion must read the real action files off disk, not a fixture string. Also run `npx playwright test e2e/` for the messages/calendar/admin flows against the local Postgres (docker ps shows it up) because these are the redirect paths a user actually walks.

title: Memory records ignore their own `sensitivity` column — a board-eyes-only knowledge card is returned to every club member AND fed to the model, while Documents are clearance-gated on the identical code path
why_open: `apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:788` gives MemoryRecord `sensitivity String @default("standard")`, and `apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:44-48` (`sensitivityRank`) plus `:94-109` (`authorizeRetrieved`) already implement the clearance ceiling. Memory never uses either. `apps/web/src/lib/memory.ts:10-14` — `canSeeMemoryCard(ctx, card: { roleId: string | null }, org)` — the card parameter is typed to carry ONLY `roleId`, so sensitivity is unrepresentable at the gate. Worse, the corpus loader never even selects it: `apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:51-54` reads `select: { id, title, content, roleId, organizationId }` for memoryRecord, while the immediately adjacent document query at `:57-65` selects `sensitivity: true` with the comment 'Dropping it from this projection silently reclassifies every document as standard'. The consequence is live on two production paths: `apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/memory/page.tsx:63` filters with `canSeeMemoryCard` alone, and `apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:95` does the same before pushing the card body into the Relay corpus that `apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:99-100` sends to the model. So a restricted card is exposed to the whole club and to a third-party model, which is exactly the source-ACL-before-model-exposure property WRK-070-006 and WRK-070-002 exist for. The governed `MemoryCandidate` review half of WRK-070-006 additionally needs a review-state column on MemoryRecord and therefore needs apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma, which is owned by another run — that half is FAIL on file ownership, name it and stop.
smallest_real_change: Widen `canSeeMemoryCard`'s card parameter from `{ roleId: string | null }` to `{ roleId: string | null; sensitivity?: string | null }` and, after the existing role/president/OSE branches pass, require `sensitivityRank(card.sensitivity) <= sensitivityRank(clearanceIn(ctx, org))` reusing the exports already in apps/web/src/lib/search.ts — do not write a second ranking. THIS WIDENS A TYPE: grep every construction site before finishing. There are exactly three real ones — apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:51-54 (add `sensitivity: true` to the select, or the field arrives undefined and ranks 0, which is the silent-reclassification failure the document comment warns about), apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[slug]/memory/page.tsx:57-63 (the findMany there must also select it), and apps/web/src/lib/memory.test.ts's fixtures. Because the field is optional, `tsc` will NOT catch a caller that forgets it, so add an assertion in search-data.itest.ts that reads a real seeded `restricted` card as an ordinary member and expects it absent — that test exercises the query, not the helper. MUTATION PROOF: (1) delete `sensitivity: true` from the search-data.ts select and confirm the itest reds (this is the mutation that proves the producer, not the helper); (2) change the comparison to `>=` and confirm memory.test.ts reds; restore both. Run the integration test against the running Postgres, not by reasoning.

title: The transactional outbox writes rows that nothing ever dispatches — `dispatchOnce` has no production caller, so duplicate / out-of-order / gap / partial-batch / stale-write behaviour is proven only against a hand-built fake
why_open: `apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts:191` defines `dispatchOnce` and `:263` defines `replay` (line numbers as of the current working tree, which a concurrent run has grown by ~120 lines); grep across apps/** and packages/** finds their only callers in apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.test.ts. Rows ARE produced — `outboxEventRow` (outbox.ts:93) is called for real at apps/web/src/app/(app)/approvals/actions.ts:155 and :437, inside the same transaction as the business write — so the table fills up and drains never. A concurrent run has just added apps/web/src/lib/outbox/consumers.ts (`consumersFor` at :160, `allConsumers` at :165) and it has no callers either, so both ends of the pipeline now exist and the loop between them does not. `apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/` contains exactly one route, `reminders`; there is no outbox job, no scheduler entry, and no implementation of the `OutboxPorts` interface anywhere in the tree. The schema is already complete and needs no change: apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma:1339-1364 has state/attempts/lastError/availableAt/deadLetteredAt and `eventId String @unique`. So every property WRK-060-005 names — duplicates (at-least-once, outbox.ts:12-20), out-of-order and gaps (backoff at outbox.ts:127-131 reorders redelivery), partial batches (`claimDue(now, limit)`), stale conditional writes (`markDispatched` after the consumer returns, outbox.ts:171-174) — is asserted only against a fake `ports()` object in the unit test, never against the atomic claim that has to hold when two ECS tasks run the same schedule. That is the 'fake test proves nothing' failure the outbox's own doc comment (outbox.ts:88-93) warns about: 'Must be atomic — two dispatchers running at once must not claim the same record.'
smallest_real_change: Reuse `consumersFor` from apps/web/src/lib/outbox/consumers.ts as the `deliver` port rather than writing a second consumer registry — that file is currently dead and this is what gives it a caller. Add `apps/web/src/lib/outbox/prisma-ports.ts` implementing `OutboxPorts` against `db`, with `claimDue` as ONE atomic statement — `db.$queryRaw` doing `UPDATE "OutboxEvent" SET state='dispatching', attempts=attempts+1 WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM "OutboxEvent" WHERE state='pending' AND "availableAt" <= $now ORDER BY "availableAt" LIMIT $limit FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING *` — because a read-then-write is the race the interface comment forbids. Add `apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/outbox/route.ts` copied in shape from apps/web/src/app/api/jobs/reminders/route.ts (same bearer check, same `parseJobRequest` envelope with an hour-window idempotencyKey, `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"`) and run the pass inside `forEachInstitution("outbox-dispatch", ...)` from apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:456 so each tenant's rows are claimed inside that tenant's scope — a single unscoped sweep would be the cross-tenant read that file exists to prevent. `deliver` starts as the in-process handler set (there is no queue yet); do not invent SQS. Then write `apps/web/src/lib/jobs/outbox-dispatch.itest.ts` against the running Postgres, modelled on apps/web/src/lib/jobs/reminders-isolation.itest.ts, covering exactly the WRK-060-005 list: two concurrent `claimDue` calls claim disjoint sets (duplicates), a record whose delivery throws comes back at a later `availableAt` while a later-written record is delivered first (out-of-order), a record that fails MAX_ATTEMPTS times dead-letters rather than vanishing (gap), `limit` smaller than the pending count leaves the remainder pending (partial batch), and `markDispatched` on a row another dispatcher already dead-lettered does not resurrect it (stale conditional write). MUTATION PROOF: replace `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` with a plain SELECT and confirm the concurrency test reds; move `markDispatched` above `deliver` (outbox.ts:171-174) and confirm the loss test reds; restore both. Run it — do not reason about it.

title: No provider/product/capability/direction is classified in the required seven-state vocabulary with evidence — the catalog uses a different, coarser lifecycle keyed to whole artifacts
why_open: The requirement names exactly seven states: PLANNED, DEVELOPMENT, CERTIFICATION_PENDING, AVAILABLE, DEGRADED, SUSPENDED, UNSUPPORTED. grep across apps/**, packages/**, tools/**, tests/**: `CERTIFICATION_PENDING` appears nowhere at all; `UNSUPPORTED` only in packages/identity/src/{logout,scim}.ts (an unrelated SCIM/logout concept); `DEGRADED` only in packages/identity/src/oidc-connection.ts and packages/provisioning/src/cell-registry.ts (cell health, not connector capability); `PLANNED` only as a tenant lifecycle state in packages/provisioning/src/lifecycle.ts:18. What exists instead is `CatalogLifecycle` at packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts:55-67 — DRAFT/SUBMITTED/CERTIFIED/PUBLISHED/DEPRECATED/REVOKED — which is a different vocabulary and, crucially, is carried on a whole `CatalogEntry` (catalogs.ts:150-169), not on a (provider, product, capability, direction) tuple. There is exactly one connector entry in the whole catalog, `RELAY_ANTHROPIC_CONNECTOR` (catalogs.ts:631-657), and it declares no products, no capabilities and no direction — so 'classify each exact provider/product/capability/direction' has no object to attach to. The evidence requirement IS partly met at the artifact level (`CatalogCertification.evidenceRefs`, catalogs.ts:110-118, refused when empty by `certificationState` at :328) — that machinery should be reused, not rebuilt. There is a real render site waiting for the answer: apps/system-studio/src/app/page.tsx:71 calls `availabilityDecisions(CATALOG_ENTRIES, availabilityScope)` and splits it into offered/refused for the operator console.
smallest_real_change: Add `packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts` declaring `ConnectorCapabilityStatus = 'PLANNED' | 'DEVELOPMENT' | 'CERTIFICATION_PENDING' | 'AVAILABLE' | 'DEGRADED' | 'SUSPENDED' | 'UNSUPPORTED'` and a `ConnectorCapability { provider, product, capability, direction: 'read' | 'write' | 'bidirectional', status, evidenceRefs: readonly string[] }`, plus `capabilityProblems()` that refuses `AVAILABLE` or `DEGRADED` with an empty `evidenceRefs` (the same rule `certificationState` already applies at catalogs.ts:328-330 — call it, do not copy it) and refuses a status whose artifact-level `isUsable` verdict disagrees (an AVAILABLE capability on an entry `isUsable` calls `uncertified` is the false-claim this requirement exists to stop). Extend `ConnectorEntry` (catalogs.ts:194-199) with a required `capabilities: readonly ConnectorCapability[]` and fill it for RELAY_ANTHROPIC_CONNECTOR with the ONE thing that actually ships — provider `anthropic`, product `messages-api`, capability `completion`, direction `write`, status `CERTIFICATION_PENDING`, evidenceRefs naming apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts and apps/web/src/lib/partition-services.ts — matching the honest posture already written at catalogs.ts:620-630. WIDENING A TYPE: `ConnectorEntry` has exactly one construction site (catalogs.ts:631) and one discriminating consumer (`isUsable`'s `entry.kind === 'connector'` branch at catalogs.ts:473); making the field required means `tsc` catches a missed site, which is the point of making it required rather than optional. Surface it: `CapabilityAvailabilityDecision` (catalogs.ts:551-560) gains the per-capability statuses so apps/system-studio/src/app/page.tsx:71-73 renders per-capability rows instead of one entry row. MUTATION PROOF: set the RELAY entry's capability status to `AVAILABLE` and confirm catalogs.test.ts reds with the disagreement reason; empty its `evidenceRefs` and confirm it reds again; restore. Assert on the value `availabilityDecisions` EMITS, not on `capabilityProblems` called directly.

title: System-of-record is declared per business DOMAIN only — there is no field/object-level authority and no sync-direction contract anywhere in the tree
why_open: packages/module-runtime/src/coexistence.ts is the whole of it. `SystemOfRecordAuthority = 'tenure' | 'external'` (coexistence.ts:65) and `SystemOfRecordMap = Readonly<Record<string, SystemOfRecordAuthority>>` (coexistence.ts:72) key on a business DOMAIN, and coexistence.ts:81 pins the key space to `PERMISSION_DOMAINS` — roughly a dozen coarse names like `finance`. `coexistenceProblems` (coexistence.ts:98-140) validates only that the profile is known, the map is non-empty, every key is a known domain and every value is one of the two authorities. Nothing anywhere models an object or a field. grep for `syncDirection` across apps/**, packages/**, tools/**, tests/** returns nothing at all; there is no `SyncDirection`, no inbound/outbound/bidirectional contract, no per-field owner. That matters concretely for the profile the file itself names: `HYBRID_PROCESS_SPLIT` (coexistence.ts:53) says 'the system of record is assigned per process/domain' and `COEXISTENCE_TRANSITION` (coexistence.ts:55) says 'controlled, bidirectional coexistence' — a bidirectional profile with no direction contract cannot state which side may write which field, which is precisely the dual-write the file's own header quote prohibits ('Dual write is prohibited unless a named reconciliation ownership protocol proves safety', coexistence.ts:13-16). Real callers exist so this is not greenfield: the declaration is consumed by packages/module-runtime/src/resolve.ts and validated through packages/provisioning/src/manifest.ts, and system-studio composes it at apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts and apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/new/ComposeForm.tsx.
smallest_real_change: Add to coexistence.ts a `SyncDirection = 'INBOUND' | 'OUTBOUND' | 'BIDIRECTIONAL' | 'NONE'` and an optional-but-validated `objectAuthority?: readonly { object: string; authority: SystemOfRecordAuthority; direction: SyncDirection; fields?: readonly { field: string; authority: SystemOfRecordAuthority }[] }[]` on `CoexistenceDeclaration` (coexistence.ts:74-77), then extend `coexistenceProblems` with the rules that make it mean something: (a) an object whose `authority` contradicts its domain's entry in `systemOfRecord` is refused — that is the invisible contradiction the file's header says decides whether a second writer reaches the ledger; (b) `BIDIRECTIONAL` is refused unless the profile is `COEXISTENCE_TRANSITION` or `HYBRID_PROCESS_SPLIT`, because those are the only two profiles that declare bidirectional coexistence; (c) a field-level entry whose authority differs from its object's requires `direction !== 'NONE'`, since a field owned by the other side with no sync channel is a field that silently never updates. WIDENING A TYPE: the field is optional, so `tsc` will not flag a caller that omits it — grep every `CoexistenceDeclaration` construction site before finishing (apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts, apps/system-studio/src/lib/adopt.ts, packages/provisioning/src/manifest.ts, packages/provisioning/src/adoption.ts and the fixtures in packages/platform-config/src/modules.test.ts and packages/provisioning/src/provisioning.test.ts) and name each one in the change. MUTATION PROOF: delete rule (a) and confirm the module-runtime test reds on a declaration where `systemOfRecord.finance='external'` but an object claims `authority:'tenure'`; delete rule (b) and confirm a `TENURE_CLOUD_PRIMARY` declaration with a BIDIRECTIONAL object stops being refused; restore. Assert through `coexistenceProblems` as the manifest validator calls it, not through a private helper.

title: The sign-in page hardcodes which methods it draws from raw env vars, and the two functions built to answer that question and to say why a connection is refused have no production caller
why_open: `cellLoginMethods` (apps/web/src/lib/auth-connections.ts:124-126) and `connectionRefusals` (apps/web/src/lib/auth-connections.ts:135-148) are exported and never imported outside apps/web/src/lib/auth-connections.test.ts — grep for both names across apps/** and packages/** returns only the definitions. Only `oktaIsUsable` reached production, at apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:28 (`const oktaConfigured = oktaIsUsable()`). Meanwhile the surface that draws the buttons ignores all of it: apps/web/src/app/signin/page.tsx:24-26 computes `const devLoginEnabled = process.env.AUTH_DEV_LOGIN === "true"` and `const passphraseRequired = Boolean(process.env.DEV_LOGIN_PASSPHRASE)` straight from the environment, and page.tsx:47 branches on that boolean alone. So the page renders a working-looking credential form from two raw env reads while the registry projection that knows whether the connection is configured, enabled and holding an unexpired credential (auth-connections.ts:113-121) is consulted by nobody drawing UI, and the refusal reasons that exist specifically so 'a connection silently absent from a sign-in page' does not get reported as 'SSO is broken' (auth-connections.ts:128-134) are never rendered anywhere. That is the exact shape WRK-030-005 forbids — a button whose presence is decided by something other than the certification/usability gate — and the exact shape WRK-GATE-110 calls untruthful connector UX.
smallest_real_change: Make the sign-in page render FROM the projection instead of from env: replace signin/page.tsx:24-26 with `const methods = cellLoginMethods()` and drive each button off an entry of `OfferedMethod` (the type `loginMethods` in @tenure/provisioning already returns), so a method that the registry refuses cannot be drawn at all. Then render `connectionRefusals()` as a short, non-alarming line under the form — one sentence per refused connection quoting `problems` — so 'configured but not offered' is visible rather than silent. Keep dev-login flowing through the same projection: it is already an `IdentityConnection` at auth-connections.ts:81-98, so it should arrive as an offered method, not as a second env read. Do NOT touch apps/web/src/components (owned by another run) — the page already imports TenureLogo/TenureWordmark and needs no component change. MUTATION PROOF: in a test, pass an env where `OKTA_ISSUER` is set but `OKTA_CLIENT_ID` is empty — `validateConnection` fails it, `oktaIsUsable` returns false — and assert the rendered method list contains no Okta entry and the refusal list names `appClientId`; then mutate signin/page.tsx to fall back to `process.env.OKTA_ISSUER` and confirm the test reds. The assertion must read what the PAGE emits, not what `cellLoginMethods` returns, or the test survives the page going back to env reads.

title: Relay tool authorization has one gate — the tool's own permission — and no action risk class, so nothing distinguishes a read from a bulk/delete/external-share/finance/HR action or requires the owning policy to pass
why_open: `authorizeRelayTools` (apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:81-126) loops the enabled modules' registrations and calls `decideCheck(world, { permission: tool.requiredPermission, resourceType: 'RelayTool', resourceId: null })` at relay-tools.ts:102-112. That is the entire decision: hold the permission, get the tool. There is no risk class, no bulk threshold, no external-share check, no delete gate, and no consultation of the owning domain's policy (finance, HR, payment, legal, safety) before a tool in that domain is offered. The contract cannot help — `ToolRegistration` (packages/contracts/src/index.ts:711-719) carries only `readOnly` and `reauthorizesPerCall`, and `parseToolRegistration` at :737-739 enforces just one coupling between them — and packages/contracts is owned by another run, so the classification has to be derived in relay-tools.ts from the permission key rather than declared in the contract. The gate has a real production caller: apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:99 calls `authorizeRelayTools` on every chat request and :100 gates retrieval on `toolOffered`. Honest scope note: modules/index.ts:464-473 registers exactly one tool today, `search.corpus`, `readOnly: true` — so the risk gate would fire on it as a read and allow it. That means the classification must be visible in what the route emits (the refusal list), not only in a branch nothing reaches, or it is a control with no subject.
smallest_real_change: Add to relay-tools.ts an `ActionRiskClass = 'READ' | 'DRAFT' | 'WRITE' | 'BULK' | 'EXTERNAL_SHARE' | 'DELETE' | 'PRIVILEGED'` and a pure `riskOf(tool: ToolRegistration): ActionRiskClass` derived from the registration's own facts — `readOnly === true` is READ; otherwise the `<module>.<action>` suffix of `requiredPermission` decides (`.delete`/`.purge` → DELETE, `.bulk`/`.import`/`.export` → BULK, `.share`/`.publish` → EXTERNAL_SHARE, and a module in the owning-policy set {finance, hr, payment, legal, safety} → PRIVILEGED). Then, before pushing to `offered` at relay-tools.ts:114-116, refuse anything above DRAFT unless the owning policy's own permission ALSO passes `decideCheck` — i.e. a PRIVILEGED tool must clear its domain's administrative permission, not merely its own — and put the risk class on `OfferedTool`/`RefusedTool` so apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts surfaces it in the response beside the existing refusal reason. WIDENING A TYPE: `OfferedTool`/`RefusedTool` (relay-tools.ts:39-50) are consumed by the chat route and by ai-kill-switch.test.ts — check both. MUTATION PROOF: add a fixture registration `finance.ledger.post` with `readOnly:false, reauthorizesPerCall:true` to the test's module set, assert it lands in `refused` with reason naming the owning finance policy for a principal who holds `finance.ledger.post` but not the finance admin permission, then mutate `riskOf` to return READ for it and confirm the test reds. Second mutation, on the PRODUCER: make the chat route drop the risk class from its response and confirm a route-level assertion reds — otherwise the property is proven only by calling `riskOf` directly and survives the route ignoring it. Do not edit packages/contracts.

title: Of the six named sinks, browser / event / audit-metadata are now guarded and log / evidence-ref / model prompt are not — the requirement's word 'Prove' is unmet for three
why_open: Re-verified against the working tree AFTER a concurrent run landed a secret scanner, so this is narrowed rather than stale. GUARDED, do not rebuild: browser — tests/security/no-tokens-in-browser-storage.test.mjs scans every tracked and untracked source file for credential vocabulary at a localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/cookie call site; events — `outboxEventRow` now calls `findSecretValues(payload, "payload")` at apps/web/src/lib/outbox/outbox.ts:113 and throws `ProviderPayloadRefused`; audit metadata — packages/audit/src/record.ts:350-351 pipes metadata through `redactSecretValues` then `redactMetadata`; identity credentials — packages/provisioning/src/identity-registry.ts:416-423 refuses a credential whose `ref` is not `arn:aws:secretsmanager:` or `/tenure/`. STILL OPEN. Logs: apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts:229 does `console.error(\`[command] ${command.action} failed:\`, err)` with the raw error object, and apps/web/src/lib/tenant-scope.ts:134-139,158-162 emit warn lines; nothing asserts a secret-shaped value cannot reach any `console.*`, and CloudWatch keeps whatever does. Evidence: `CatalogCertification.evidenceRefs` (packages/provisioning/src/catalogs.ts:110-118) is a free `readonly string[]` whose doc comment says 'By reference, never inline' at :113 and whose only validation, `certificationState` at :328-330, checks length only. Model: apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts assembles the prompt sent to api.anthropic.com — the one egress the platform makes — and nothing screens what goes into it. title: Suspend/hibernate/reactivate/offboard/purge are a real state machine, but owner-departure does not exist and residual cost is prose that nothing reconciles against retained resources
why_open: The lifecycle half is genuinely done and should not be rebuilt: packages/provisioning/src/lifecycle.ts:13-42 declares SUSPENDING/SUSPENDED_LOGICAL/HIBERNATING/HIBERNATED_ZERO_RUNTIME/REACTIVATING/EXPORTING/OFFBOARDING/LEGAL_HOLD/PURGE_PENDING/PURGING/PURGED_ZERO_INCREMENTAL_COST, `TRANSITIONS` at :50-89 makes each reachable from one place, `REQUIRES_APPROVAL` at :98-105 makes PURGE_PENDING→PURGING need a recorded approver, and `advance` at :200 enforces it. Two of the requirement's clauses are open. (a) Owner departure: grep for `owner-departure`, `ownerDeparture` and `ownerSuccession` across apps/**, packages/**, tests/** returns NOTHING; the only succession in the tree is seat succession for club officers (packages/organization-model/src/succession-release.ts, continuity.ts), which is about a role inside a tenant, not about the person who owns a tenant or a connection departing. (b) Residual reconciliation: `RESIDUAL_COST` (lifecycle.ts:122-131) is a `Record<TenantState, string>` of English sentences — 'snapshots, retained object storage, audit evidence and any dedicated edge resources continue to bill' — and its only consumers render that string: apps/system-studio/src/lib/tenant-state.ts, apps/system-studio/src/lib/fleet-health.ts, apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/page.tsx and .../[slug]/page.tsx. Nothing compares the sentence to what is actually retained, so a HIBERNATED tenant still running a dedicated resource the sentence does not mention is displayed exactly like one that is not — which is the '$0 that is not $0' failure the comment at lifecycle.ts:115-121 says the map exists to prevent. Ownership note: cost ALLOCATION lives in packages/finops (owned by another run) — keep the reconciliation in packages/provisioning and consume finops read-only if at all.
smallest_real_change: Turn `RESIDUAL_COST` from prose into a checkable claim without losing the prose. Add `packages/provisioning/src/residual-reconciliation.ts` with `ResidualClaim { state: TenantState; retains: readonly ResourceClass[]; note: string }` where `ResourceClass` enumerates what a cell can actually hold (`compute`, `database`, `object-storage`, `snapshot`, `audit-evidence`, `edge`), re-express the five existing entries as claims keeping their exact sentences as `note`, and add `reconcileResidual(claim, observed: readonly ResourceClass[])` returning `{ unexplained: ResourceClass[]; overclaimed: ResourceClass[] }` — an observed class the claim does not list is the bill nobody expected, and a claimed class that is absent is a console telling an operator they are paying for something they are not. Then add owner departure as a lifecycle fact rather than a new subsystem: an `ownerPrincipalId` on the advance options (lifecycle.ts:163) and a refusal in `advance` when a tenant is moved into SUSPENDING/HIBERNATING/OFFBOARDING with no successor owner recorded, so a departure cannot silently orphan a tenant — the same shape `REQUIRES_APPROVAL` already uses for PURGE_PENDING→PURGING. Wire the reconciliation into apps/system-studio/src/lib/tenant-state.ts so the console renders `unexplained` beside the note rather than the note alone. MUTATION PROOF: give a HIBERNATED_ZERO_RUNTIME fixture an observed `compute` resource and confirm provisioning.test.ts reds when `reconcileResidual` is mutated to return an empty `unexplained`; drop the successor-owner refusal from `advance` and confirm the departure test reds; restore both. Assert on what `advance` and the console projection emit, not on the helper in isolation.

title: WCAG 2.2 AA / keyboard / screen-reader / reflow / high-contrast / reduced-motion / RTL / density matrices for the connector surfaces — FAIL on file ownership, not on merit
